app.name: mcp-news
app.tagline: Your news, ranked by rules you wrote.
common.name: Name
tier.label: Level {tier}
tier.0.name: Collect
tier.0.desc: No AI model is configured. Everything still works: articles are collected, de-duplicated, stored, keyword-searched and ranked against your interests.
tier.1.name: Index
tier.1.desc: An embedding model is configured, so search understands meaning as well as words.
tier.2.name: Understand
tier.2.desc: Both an embedding and a chat model are configured, so translation, summaries and questions are available.
setup.title: Welcome
setup.welcome.title: Set up your news feed
setup.welcome.body: This takes about two minutes. You will choose a language, where your articles are kept, which sources to read, and what you are interested in. You can change all of it later, and you never need to edit a file.
setup.welcome.privacy: Everything stays on this machine. Nothing you do here is sent anywhere.
setup.language.title: Language
setup.language.body: Which language should this application use?
setup.language.help: This changes the words in the application. It does not filter the news itself — you choose sources in the next steps, and each source has its own language.
setup.storage.title: Where to keep your articles
setup.storage.body: Articles and their full text are stored in a folder on this machine. Pick somewhere with a few gigabytes free that you can find again.
setup.storage.help: The database folder holds one file containing every article's title, link and score. The archive folder holds the full saved text, which grows more quickly. They can be the same place. If you are running this in Docker, only folders that were made available to the container can be used — the test button below tells you straight away.
setup.storage.docker_note: Running inside Docker. To use a folder on your own computer, add it to the volumes section of docker-compose.yml and restart, then come back here.
setup.bundles.title: Choose what to read
setup.bundles.body: Each bundle is a small, reviewed list of feeds. Turn on what interests you. You can add your own sources at any time.
setup.bundles.help: A bundle is just a file listing feeds, with the date each was last checked. Turning one on adds its sources; turning it off later leaves the articles you already collected in place.
setup.bundles.none_selected: Choose at least one bundle so there is something to read.
setup.profile.title: What are you interested in?
setup.profile.body: These rules decide the order of your feed. Write a few subjects and the words that would appear in an article about each.
setup.profile.help: Nothing is hidden here. An article's position is the sum of the rules that matched it, and every article in your feed shows which rules those were. Specific words work far better than common ones: lithography tells you something, technology does not.
setup.profile.match_placeholder: Words that would appear, separated by commas
setup.done.title: Ready
setup.done.body: Your settings are saved. Collection starts now; the first articles usually appear within a minute or two.
today.title: Today
today.empty: Nothing has scored above your threshold in this window yet. Try a longer window, add more sources, or lower the threshold in Settings.
today.collecting: Collecting for the first time. This page fills in as articles arrive.
today.end: That is all {count} items above your threshold. Nothing further is being held back.
today.end.one: That is the only item above your threshold. Nothing further is being held back.
search.title: Search
search.mode_note: Search is matching words only, because no embedding model is configured. Add one in Settings to search by meaning.
search.empty: Nothing matched. Try fewer or more common words.
article.no_body: No readable text was saved for this article. Open the original to read it.
sources.title: Sources
sources.add.title: Add a source
sources.test.ok: Working. Found {count} recent items, the newest is {title}.
sources.help: A source is one feed address that is checked on a schedule. Test before you add: the test fetches the feed once and shows you what it found, without saving anything.
sources.help.interval: How often this feed is checked. Shorter is not better — most publishers update a few times an hour at most, and checking too often is impolite and can get you blocked.
sources.help.status: On means it is being checked. Off keeps it in your list but stops checking it. Superseded means the feed moved and a replacement is listed. Dead means it stopped responding and is kept only so its history still makes sense.
sources.empty: No sources yet. Add one, or turn on a bundle in Settings.
sources.delete_confirm: Remove {name} from your list? Articles already collected are kept.
profile.title: Your interests
profile.body: These rules are the whole ranking. Edit them and your feed reorders immediately.
profile.rule.name: Name
profile.help.match: Any one of these words appearing in an article makes this rule fire. Words are matched whole, so a rule for Ace will not match surface or peace. Separate them with commas.
profile.help.must_include: A safety net for ambiguous names. If you fill this in, the rule only fires when one of these words is also present. Useful when a company shares its name with an ordinary word.
profile.help.exclude: The opposite. If any of these words appears, the rule does not fire at all.
profile.help.weight: How much this matters, from 1 for mildly interesting to 5 for tell me straight away. A rule's contribution is its importance multiplied by how many times it matched.
profile.help.in_title_multiplier: How much more a match in the headline counts than one buried in the body. A headline usually says what the article is about, so the default of 2 is a reasonable starting point.
profile.help.mute: Anything matching these is scored zero and never appears, however well it matches elsewhere.
profile.help.sources: A multiplier applied to every article from that website. Above 1 promotes it, below 1 demotes it.
profile.preview.note: Showing what your feed would look like with these unsaved changes.
profile.help.threshold: Articles below this score are still collected and searchable, they are just kept out of the Today list.
profile.cap: Most any one rule can contribute
profile.help.cap: Stops one repeated name from swamping everything else. A rule that matches twenty times still contributes at most this much.
profile.help.half_life: How quickly an article slides down the Today list as it ages. At the half-life it counts for half as much. This is applied only when the feed is displayed — the stored score never changes, so searching your history still works.
settings.title: Settings
settings.language.label: Application language
settings.language.help: Changes the words in this application. Restarting is not needed.
settings.storage.help: Where your database and saved article text live. Changing these takes effect after a restart; existing files are not moved for you.
settings.collection.help: How often the whole source list is swept. Each source also has its own minimum interval, which is never exceeded.
settings.collection.help_concurrency: How many feeds are fetched at the same time. Higher is faster and less polite. Requests to the same website are always spaced out regardless of this number.
settings.collection.robots: Respect robots.txt when fetching article text
settings.collection.help_robots: Publishers use a file called robots.txt to say which automated visitors they welcome. Leaving this on is the courteous default.
settings.collection.fulltext: Fetch the full text of articles
settings.collection.help_fulltext: Most feeds carry only a summary. With this on, the article page is fetched once and its readable text saved, so search covers the whole piece and you can read it later even if the page disappears.
settings.providers.help: Entirely optional. With no model configured this application still collects, de-duplicates, searches and ranks. A model adds search by meaning, translation and summaries. Any OpenAI-compatible server works, including one running on your own machine.
settings.providers.api_key_env: Name of the environment variable holding the key
settings.providers.help_api_key_env: Keys are never stored in a settings file. Put the key in your environment or .env file, and write the name of that variable here.
settings.providers.help_chains: Each request tries these in order and moves to the next when one is unreachable. Putting a local model first keeps your reading private and costs nothing.
settings.providers.none: No model configured. Running at level 0.
settings.about.no_auth: This application ships no login and makes no claim to be secure on a network. It listens only on this machine unless you deliberately put it behind your own reverse proxy.
settings.about.config_location: Your settings are plain files in {path}. You never need to open them, but they are yours and they are readable.
settings.reset.confirm: Run the setup wizard again? Your articles and sources are kept.
status.title: Status
err.setup.required: Setup has not been completed yet.
err.setup.invalid: Some answers were missing or invalid.
err.path.cannot_create: That folder could not be created.
err.path.not_writable: That folder exists but cannot be written to.
err.source.unreachable: The feed could not be fetched.
err.source.unparseable: That address responded, but it is not a feed this application understands.
err.source.empty: That feed was read, but it contains no items.
err.source.duplicate_id: A source with that name already exists.
err.source.bad_url: That does not look like a web address.
err.profile.invalid: Your interests could not be saved: {detail}
err.busy: A collection run is already in progress.
